cohort: 9,038 women undergoing trial of labor after cesarean (TOLAC) between 2005 and 2019
finding: While both prior VD and prior VBAC increased the likelihood of successful TOLAC, prior VBAC was a better predictor of success and was associated with a significantly lower risk of uterine rupture compared to no prior VD or prior VD alone.
mod_finding: Women with prior vaginal birth after cesarean (VBAC) and prior vaginal delivery showed significantly higher rates of successful VBAC compared to those with no prior vaginal delivery or VBAC.
